items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Louis Armstrong, Dizzy, you name it.

ctx.x: Was he doing Louis Armstrong at that time?

Louis Armstrong, Dizzy, you name it. Especially trumpet players. He had Red Allen and Higginbotham and that group, the Dixieland groups. He had control over all of these different groups — Billie Holiday and you name it — Dinah Washington, he had all of these people. And so I got to know him first by just sending, make sure I sent that commission into him. So he sort of got a respect for me as a business person. So in 1944

we got a job to go to 52nd Street and open in the Onyx Club. And in those days they gave you a long term deal, so the deal was for six months. And Jimmy Jones, I’m sort of ahead of myself, because actually Jimmy Jones joined the group — Raymond Walters was the first pianist with us, and he worked with us maybe in Chicago for maybe about two or three months. And then Jimmy Jones and I had been friends, I knew him as a player and I recommended that he come on with us. And that’s how the real Stuff Smith Trio got…
